security_spec.violation_condition: sctrctl/vsctrctl read path in RTL directly returns mctrctl hardware register state without applying the correct per-CSR read mask. The sctrctl read mask (0x787F9F80000DC3) excludes bit 2 (M field) and bit 9 (MTE field) present in the mctrctl mask (0x787F9F80000FC7). If the Chisel CSR module implements sctrctl as a simple alias that reads the raw mctrctl wire without masking, S-mode and VS-mode can observe M-mode CTR enable and M-mode trap enable bits, leaking M-mode configuration state to lower privilege levels.
security_spec.summary: sctrctl/vsctrctl alias mctrctl in hardware but have narrower read masks (missing M, MTE bits); returning raw mctrctl state without per-CSR masking leaks M-mode-only configuration fields to S/VS-mode via CSR read instructions

findings.finding: sctrctl (0x14E) and vsctrctl (0x24E) CSR address constants are defined and added to the all-CSRs lookup list (lines 523, 546, 619), but no CSRModule is instantiated for them in SupervisorLevel.scala, VirtualSupervisorLevel.scala, or MachineLevel.scala. The NewCSR framework (NewCSR.scala:1021) treats unregistered addresses as illegal-instruction. The vulnerability described in the security spec — sctrctl read path returning raw mctrctl state without masking bits 2 (M) and 9 (MTE) — cannot be assessed because no read path exists.

spec_citations.excerpt: The sctrctl register provides supervisor mode access to a subset of mctrctl. Bits 2 and 9 in sctrctl are read-only 0. As a result, the M and MTE fields in mctrctl are not accessible through sctrctl.
All fields are optional except for M, S, U, and BPFRZ. All unimplemented fields are read-only 0, while all implemented fields are writable.

findings.finding: The CSR read/write dispatch map (csrRwMap at line 320) contains no entry for sctrctl (0x14E), vsctrctl (0x24E), mctrctl (0x34E), sctrstatus (0x14F), or sctrdepth (0x15F). The noCSRIllegal logic catches unregistered CSR addresses, so accesses to these CSRs raise an illegal-instruction exception. No information leak is possible because the registers cannot be read at all.
findings.snippet:
private val noCSRIllegal = (ren || wen) && Cat(csrRwMap.keys.toSeq.sorted.map(csrAddr => !(addr === csrAddr.U))).andR
